findings.issue: Nothing checks that replay mode with --lineup actually plays the line-up policies (A-5 / REQ-062.2: the suggested Replay line must reproduce a line-up hand). The only replay tests use --size 3, where lineUpPolicyFactory falls back to the same random moves as defaultPolicyFactory, so the replay output is identical either way.
findings.evidence: Mutation: in src/playtest/cli.ts:325 I replaced `preset === undefined || seams.makePolicy !== undefined` with `true || ...` so replay always ignored the line-up. tests/playtest/cli.test.ts and tests/playtest/lineup.acceptance.test.ts still passed (11 passed, 1 skipped). The current code is correct: a probe showed that 30 of 30 Mixed 6-max hands replayed identically through lineUpPolicyFactory, and 23 of 30 differed from the default policies, so a test at 6 seats would be able to tell the two apart.
findings.fix: In the '--lineup parsing, header lines and replay suffix' test, play a 6-seat line-up hand: take a hand from runPlaytest({hands: N, seed: 42, size: 6, lineUp: 'Mixed'}, onHand) whose actions differ from the default policies, run main(['--replay-code', code, '--button', b, '--stacks', ..., '--lineup', 'mixed']), and assert that the printed hand equals formatHand of the run's hand (or that the action lines differ from the same replay without --lineup).

findings.issue: The rule 'a line-up replaces makePolicy unless an explicit seam is set' is written twice: in runPlaytest (src/playtest/runner.ts:313-316) and again in main's replay branch.
findings.evidence: Both blocks read `x === undefined || seams.makePolicy !== undefined ? seams : { ...seams, makePolicy: lineUpPolicyFactory(x, size) }`.
findings.fix: Export a small `lineUpSeams(seams, lineUp, size)` from runner.ts and call it from both places, or have playHand take the optional lineUp through HandSetup, so the precedence rule lives in one place.

findings.issue: `String(s.name)`, `String(s.style)` and `String(lineUpName)` only hide nulls and undefineds that can't happen here. They make the reader wonder whether 'null' could ever be printed.
findings.evidence: lineUpLines filters to kind === 'bot', so name and style are non-null. lineUpName is only used when preset is defined.
findings.fix: Pass `preset.toLowerCase()` inside lineUpLines instead of a separate name argument, and narrow bots with a type guard (or use `as string`, as lineup.ts does).

summary: The implementation matches the spec. The presets follow R-1..R-4 for every size from 2 to 10 and every user seat, with clockwise wrap. Tough heads-up seats one TAG. Names come from BOT_NAMES in fixed order, so they're unique. The CLI accepts only exact lowercase names and uses an Object.hasOwn guard ('toString' is tested). decideStyle is a straight move of the worker dispatch, and a mutation swapping Maniac and Calling station fails 4 tests. The baseline SHA is aacd5e94...e01, unchanged (re-run). Replay with --lineup reproduces hands (probe: 30 of 30). The new every-push cost is about 5.3 s in sweeps plus about 2.4 s in unit, close to the spec's estimate. AC#8 is opt-in via it.runIf(SLOW) and listed in test:slow. New src code is covered by non-acceptance unit files. One MAJOR finding: no test pins that CLI replay with --lineup uses the line-up policies, because the only replay tests use size 3, where the fallback hides the difference. The 13-file count (advice-service.test.ts, required by SPEC-07) is justified.
